The test image shows a young soybean seedling with stem/hypocotyl damage near the soil line — brownish-gray discoloration on the stem with what appears to be small dark specks. Key features: seedling stage, stem lesion at soil line, grayish-brown coloring.

Top candidates: Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora, Pythium, Charcoal_Rot. Let me view reference images.
Based on my analysis of the test image and reference images, let me view two more to confirm:

**Analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Young soybean seedling at very early growth stage
- Reddish-brown to brownish-gray discoloration on the stem/hypocotyl at/near the soil line
- Leaves remain green and intact (no foliar disease)
- Typical "damping off" presentation with stem damage at soil line

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reference shows reddish-brown, sunken, firm, dry lesions on the hypocotyl at the soil line — strongly matches the test image (similar seedling size, lesion location, and color)
- **Phytophthora**: Shows darker brown girdle extending from taproot up; plants more wilted/dead — less match
- **Pythium**: Shows water-soaked soft rot, very complete damping off of tiny seedlings — lesion character doesn't match (test image looks firmer/drier)
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Gray/charcoal coloring on more mature plants — wrong growth stage
- **Anthracnose/SDS**: Mature plant diseases affecting pods or leaf tissue — no match

The reddish-brown, firm, dry hypocotyl lesion at the soil line on a young seedling is the hallmark of Rhizoctonia seedling blight.
